react_result.final_narrative_text: The eight differentially abundant metabolites form a coordinated signal across arachidonic acid metabolism and its downstream eicosanoid branches. Three independent enrichment paradigms converge on a single dominant biological story: widespread perturbation of the arachidonic acid cascade. RaMP ORA against the merged pathway database identifies 'Eicosanoid synthesis' (WP:WP167) as the top-ranked pathway with an FDR of 3.11e-15 and a fold-enrichment of 2001-fold, driven by five of the eight input metabolites. MetaboAnalystR PSEA independently confirms 'Arachidonic acid metabolism' (KEGG:hsa00590) at p = 2.49e-06 with four overlapping compounds. The m/z-direct mummichog analysis ranks 'Arachidonic acid metabolism' first (p = 0.000168) with fourteen matched network nodes, and also hits 'Leukotriene metabolism' (rank 4, p = 0.024) and 'Prostaglandin formation from arachidonate' (rank 5, p = 0.033). Arachidonic acid (CHEBI:15843) serves as the central substrate for all three downstream enzymatic arms — the 5-lipoxygenase pathway generating leukotriene A4 and 5-HETE, the 12/15-lipoxygenase arm producing 15-HETE, and the cyclooxygenase pathway whose downstream J-series cyclopentenone includes 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-prostaglandin J2. The concurrent elevation of 5,6-EET (an epoxide formed by CYP epoxygenases) alongside the classic lipoxygenase products suggests multi-pathway activation of the arachidonic acid cascade. The phenylpropanoid derivatives (4-hydroxybenzoic acid, 3,4-dihydroxybenzeneacetic acid) did not map to eicosanoid pathways and likely represent unrelated metabolic noise or a minor co-incidental perturbation.
